agent.name: Emerging Technology Diffusion Agent
agent.specialty: Rogers diffusion analysis and context-sensitive timing implications

analytical_question: What diffusion/timing judgment follows for the same coding-assistant test/documentation task in a conservative firm with limited security-review capacity?
general_et_finding: UNCHANGED from primary: high self-reported exposure/use in 2025 developer/technology-professional survey samples, but Stack Overflow's 84% includes use OR intent and DORA's 90% measures broad AI at work in a different sample. No justified adopter-category classification or saturation estimate for mid-size SaaS firms.
application_finding: Exact peer adoption of reviewed tests/docs remains unmeasured. Rogers attributes: relative advantage=MIXED (unmeasured quality-adjusted savings); compatibility=UNFAVORABLE for this constrained setting (confidentiality restrictions); complexity=UNFAVORABLE until reviewers/security capacity exist; trialability=MIXED (technically reversible code, potentially irreversible data exposure); observability=MIXED (possible quality/cycle-time metrics, no baseline). Ratings are contextual inferences, not measured causal evidence. Accelerator: visible tools and champions plausible; inhibitors: trust, scarce security bandwidth, data policy.
organization_specific_finding: A conservative posture and irreversible confidentiality consequence change acceptable timing, not external diffusion facts: delay any use of proprietary repository content until security review, approved tool/data boundaries and reviewer capacity exist. A policy-safe synthetic-code tabletop test could precede a production-connected pilot. Revisit within six months.

evidence.claim: 84% used or planned AI tools, compared with 76% in 2024.
evidence.notes: Use plus intent, no peer or task denominator.

evidence.claim: DORA reported AI use at work by 90% of nearly 5,000 surveyed technology professionals.
evidence.notes: Different population/question; external signal held constant.

evidence.claim: 29% of 2025 respondents trusted output accuracy, down from 40% in 2024.
evidence.notes: Trust is not measured incident rate.

contrary_evidence_or_limitations: Survey use rises while trust falls.
Weak claim rejected: early-majority status in mid-size B2B SaaS firms; no representative firm denominator or time series.
No source measures reviewed test/documentation workflow prevalence among peers; 2025 sources may be stale in 2026.
confidence_and_uncertainty: Moderate for diffusion in surveyed workers; low for exact application and category. High confidence in conditional governance logic but unknown actual firm policy and available staff in this hypothetical case.
value_opportunity_implication: Potential drafting savings remain unproven; delay imposes opportunity cost but protects confidentiality while prerequisites are absent.
risk_governance_implication: Prohibit uploading proprietary code until contract, retention, data-use and access controls are approved. Human checks alone cannot undo upstream disclosure.
recommendation_management_implication: Security and engineering should complete policy/tool due diligence first; confine immediate learning to synthetic non-sensitive samples. Reassess a gated production-data trial only after controls and review staffing exist; no full adoption recommendation.
change_monitoring_triggers: Security signs off approved data boundaries and budgeted reviewer capacity.
A synthetic trial documents acceptable quality and auditability.
Refresh original surveys within 90 days; acquire two comparable peer case studies with workflow detail.
Review at six months or on confidentiality-policy change.
abstention_or_more_information_needed: No company-wide adoption-stage or peer-market-share estimate.
Do not authorize proprietary-code pilot without verified security, contracts and capacity.
Need baseline metrics and incident escalation plan.
